title: Hormuz Oil Shipments Hit Six-Month High, US Commander Says
summary: Oil and liquefied natural gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz in the past two weeks reached the highest level in six months, signaling that US naval protection and mine clearance efforts are “paying off,” a regional US commander said.

title: Companies Avoid Selling the Bonds Investors Crave: Credit Weekly
summary: Investors are clamoring for the kind of debt companies are reluctant to sell now: longer-term bonds.

title: Trump Reignites Kennedy Center Fight
summary: President Donald Trump’s plans for the Kennedy Center are hitting legal roadblocks as questions mount over the landmark’s future. Bloomberg’s Shaquille Omari breaks down the escalating battle over one of Washington’s most iconic cultural institutions. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Turkey Detains Top Finance Executives in Funds Scheme, NTV Says
summary: Turkish authorities on Saturday detained high-profile finance executives as part of an investigation into a “ponzi-like” funds scheme.

title: Bloomberg This Weekend 09/19/2026
summary: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by Brookings Institution VP and Director of Foreign Policy Program Suzanne Maloney, Signum Global Advisors Senior Partner & Fmr. US Embassy London Deputy Chief of Mission Lew Lukens, Merrill Head of CIO Market Strategy & BofA Private Bank Joe Quinlan, Vanity Fair Contributing Writer Chris Whipple, Utah Gov. & “Off Ramp” Author Spencer Cox and NYC Dept. of Consumer and Worker Protection Commissioner Sam Levine. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
summary: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini and David Gura as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)

title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
summary: Immersive movie screening, the plea for headphones, all-you-can-drink German method coming to the US, and old rock stars still rocking: Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini as they go over interesting headlines from this week. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: New York Builds Data Team to Target Consumer Ripoffs
summary: New York City is building a 36-person bureau of data scientists, technologists and economists to analyze company records for potential violations involving pricing, wages and other consumer and worker protections. NYC Consumer and Worker Protection Commissioner Sam Levine tells David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend that the effort is designed to give the city the technical expertise to enforce existing laws as algorithms and AI play a growing role in how companies set prices and compensation. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Governor Cox Says Americans Need Healthier Conflict
summary: Utah Governor Spencer Cox joins Bloomberg This Weekend and argues Americans need more substantive disagreement without the contempt he says is fueling polarization, damaged relationships and political violence. In his new book, Off Ramp, Cox calls for healthier political conflict and stronger local connections while also arguing that policymakers need more expertise to address emerging challenges such as AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Saudi Arabia Billionaires’ Family Office Dubai Bet Adds to London Exodus
summary: An investment firm for one of Saudi Arabia’s richest families is relocating from London to Dubai, according to people familiar with the matter, the latest example of private wealth outflows from the UK to the Gulf despite heightened uncertainty from the Iran war.

title: SpaceX’s Nasdaq 100 Weight Is Confirmed at 2.82% in Rebalance
summary: SpaceX will make up 2.82% of the Nasdaq 100 when the index’s quarterly rebalance takes effect Monday, according to data obtained by Bloomberg, locking in a sharp increase from its current weighting of about 1.28%.

title: Diesel Prices Keep Pressure on Fed and Markets
summary: The Federal Reserve unanimously raised its benchmark rate by a quarter point as policymakers confront inflation that remains above target and uncertainty tied to geopolitical developments. Merrill and Bank of America Head of CIO Market Strategy Joe Quinlan tells Bloomberg This Weekend hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that elevated diesel prices are a particular concern for businesses and could keep pressure on the Fed to raise rates further. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Mozambique Cut by Moody’s on Heightened Restructuring Risks
summary: Moody’s Ratings cut its assessment of Mozambique’s creditworthiness deeper into junk, citing increased risk that the gas-rich southeast African nation will restructure its sole eurobond.

title: US Greenland Deal Shifts Focus to Investment
summary: A new security agreement between the US, Denmark and Greenland would expand the American military role while preserving Greenlandic sovereignty, shifting attention toward potential US investment in mining, infrastructure and tourism. Former US diplomat Lewis Lukens tells David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend that Greenland welcomes investment but faces formidable obstacles including limited transportation infrastructure, a small workforce and the high cost of developing projects in the Arctic. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: UN Talks Offer a New Opening on Iran War
summary: World leaders head to the UN General Assembly as Gulf states seek renewed diplomacy to reduce attacks, restore more predictable energy flows and move the Iran war away from active conflict. Suzanne Maloney of the Brookings Institution joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend and says disruptions to Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and other regional infrastructure are adding urgency to those efforts as Gulf economies face mounting pressure from the conflict. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump Moves to Bar Three News Outlets From White House
summary: President Donald Trump says he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House over coverage he calls “fake news,” though questions remain about how the restrictions would be enforced and whether they could face legal challenges. Bloomberg News White House Correspondent Jeff Mason joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend and discusses how this move comes as Trump also faces protests over the future of the Kennedy Center and prepares to address the UN General Assembly with the Iran war expected to be a major focus. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Buffett Son Takes Chair as Berkshire Transition Ends
summary: Warren Buffett has stepped down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman after more than six decades at the company, becoming chairman emeritus as his son Howard takes over the board and Greg Abel remains CEO. Bloomberg News Insurance Reporter Alex Rajbhandari explains that Howard Buffett, a Berkshire director since 1993, is tasked with safeguarding the company’s culture and values as the conglomerate completes its long-planned leadership transition. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: AI Agents Test the Limits of Human Oversight
summary: OpenAI disclosed six cases of unexpected or concerning model behavior as AI companies grapple with how to monitor increasingly autonomous agents and whether stronger independent oversight is needed. Joining David Gura on Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg News AI Reporter Shirin Ghaffary explains that the safety debate is taking on geopolitical urgency as President Donald Trump emphasizes maintaining the US lead over China while resisting calls to slow AI development. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: JPMorgan Sees No Clear Endgame for Oil Markets
summary: An attack on Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline has disrupted a crucial route around the Strait of Hormuz, threatening crude deliveries to Europe and adding pressure to already tight diesel markets. On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Economics Statecraft Lead Chris Kennedy discusses how JPMorgan says it no longer has a baseline view for oil markets as the Iran conflict, attacks on Russian energy infrastructure, and uncertainty over Chinese demand make the outlook increasingly difficult to model. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Can India Turn Its Promise Into Prosperity?
summary: Blackstone COO Jon Gray says India’s young population, expanding middle class and improving infrastructure are drawing interest from global investors. But India’s demographic advantage also creates pressure: millions of young people graduate every year, while formal-sector job creation has not kept pace with their skills and expectations. At the same time, Indian states are competing aggressively for investment by cutting regulatory barriers, building industrial infrastructure and targeting sectors from electronics to semiconductors. The question is whether India can turn its scale, talent and investment momentum into enough productive jobs to sustain its growth.  (Source: Bloomberg)
